payload.text: Orchestrator decision 2026-11-12 on limit 2: keep the anchored rules. On Claude Code 2.1.322 they newly deny 8 forms: git push -d origin branch, git push origin -d branch, git push -q origin -d branch, git push upstream -d branch, git push origin +main, git push -u origin +main, git push --set-upstream origin +main, git -C . push upstream +main. Known false denies, kept as named expected denies in the fixture: git push -o "see origin +1" origin main, git push -o "see origin -d x" origin main, git push origin main -o "ask origin +1". Reason: a push whose option text spells 'origin +' or 'origin -d ' is not an ordinary push; a false deny is loud while a missed force push or remote delete is silent and may not be reversible; the shipped catalog already accepts the same kind of false deny for --delete in option text. A real ordinary push denied in use reopens this decision; the rule is not loosened without it.

payload.acceptance_criteria: When the native probe runs on the shipped catalog, git push --mirror origin, git push --prune origin, git push other +main, git push origin main +topic, git push origin branch -d, git push -uf origin main and git push origin "+main" shall be denied, and every ordinary push case in the fixture shall still run.
payload.description:
## Context
When basicly-f2zwd26 closed the push -d and plus-refspec gaps on Claude Code 2.1.322, the probe left these forms open: --mirror, --prune, remote names other than origin and upstream, a second + refspec (git push origin main +topic), a trailing -d (git push origin branch -d), clustered -uf, and quoted "+main". Infix forms for --mirror and --prune deny push options that contain those words. Same probe, no loosening, ordinary pushes must stay allowed.
